items.d: By the Bonny Jetty where seafood is sold.
These two hikes can be combined in a loop that delivers some of the best scenery from any five-mile hike in the park. Do the lake first, before you get tired from the dome climb.
The cable car also features as bungee jumping platform for a 43 m fall. The cable on the other hand is used for the zipline experience. Both over the picturesque Gauja valley.
The national archives are housed in an interesting circular building with an ogival cupola.
Alajuela's Central Cathedral is the very center of the town as is traditional in colonial Spanish urban planning. The church is pretty, but not a spectacular piece of architecture.
The sign is missing: you go through iron gates on the corner. Mostly photographic exhibits which concentrate on the Agadir earthquake on 29 February 1960.

A discovery centre with interactive and colourful displays where you can learn about the rainforest's wildlife including the reptiles that live in the Daintree River (yes, that includes snakes and crocs), the endangered…
On the banks of the river (near the city stadium), this 5.6 acres of parkland offer a pleasant and relaxing environment to stroll or to sit and watch the river flow by.
The Sokolski Monastery is a Bulgarian Orthodox monastery founded in 1833 and named after its founder Yosif Sokolski. It is in the Bulgarka Nature Park and is close to the Sokolovo cave.
Pumpkin Island off the Capricorn Coast near Yeppoon is a sparkling jewel nestled within the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park.

Fourteen giant's kettles, including three very deep ones, can be found on the Sukulanrakka hill slopes near the island of Rautiosaari. Nature trail with stairs, partly rough. No public transportation.

This relatively new church is dedicated to St. Jude Thaddeus, patron saint of lost causes. It is notable for its richly decorated, gold-toned Baroque-style altar, ceiling mural, and Divine Mercy shrine.
This impressive fortress was first built in 1670-1675 as a residence for Imam Sultan bin Saif Al Ya'arubi, and was a centre of learning for medicine, astrology and Islamic studies.

The largest cathedral in Central America and a UNESCO World Heritage site, built in a mix of baroque and neoclassical styles. The thick, low-slung, fortress-like walls were explicitly engineered to survive earthquakes.
This museum hosts artifacts from the history of computers, including Italy's oldest computer built in the end of the 1950s, and a collection of mechanical calculators from the early 1900s.

n.it: Museo degli strumenti per il calcolo

items.d: Remains of a 1790 fort built to protect the harbour.

Half fortress and half palace, this construction is a good example of mannerist architecture. Highlights include the Noble Salon (Salão Nobre), the Green Room (Sala Verde), the Audience Hall (Sala de Audiências), and the gardens.
palace with hieroglyphic inscriptions.
The building of the Yeshiva built in 1901. Since 1980, it has been used by Jews as a yeshiva once again.

Commemorates the 6,300 students who were conscripted to work in munitions factories and killed by the atomic bomb. There are statues of doves scattered throughout its five levels; at the base is a beautiful Kannon statue, always…

n.en: Memorial Tower to the Mobilized Students

items.d: A new cultural heritage museum and venue space.

One of several churches on the island but the only one completely standing, last renovated in 1934. It was built in 1360 under Serbian King Vukašin. It was built of brick and stone. The frescoes inside are not too well-preserved.
It houses spectacled alligators, paiches (the biggest freshwater fish in the Amazon basin and one of the longest fish in the world), and the Victoria amazonica (the biggest lily-pad in the world).
Massive landmark next to Mercado del Puerto, hosting the Uruguayan customs administration.
A gallery with regularly changing exhibitions in a variety of forms, sometimes modern, sometimes more traditional. Well worth a visit.
The park service keeps sled dogs for use in the winter, and during the summer offers daily demonstrations for visitors. Demonstrations are at 10AM, 2PM, and 4PM and last for 30 minutes.

in.fr: parc national et réserve du Denali

items.d: A live operating "organic farm" that has expansive grape and corn fields. In the fall you can enter the fields and pick as many fresh grapes as you want and watch how the Chinese process corn.
Terrace has an incredible view over the medina if you are willing to pay 30 dirham for a glass of tea in order to access it.
Paintings and sculptures by local artists and antiques donated by wealthy Cebuanos.
There are 300-year-old Banyan trees and a variety of sub-tropical plants in a park setting.

Opened in August 2025, this 90-hectare complex is one of the largest exhibition venues in Southeast Asia. Its centrepiece is the domed Kim Quy hall, which holds ten exhibition halls under one roof, while the surrounding outdoor…
The chapel constructed in the 15th century in the yard of Jame mosque
Massive artwork made up of a tightly packed cluster of hillside homes painted in bold colors.

Castelliani House, named after its architect. This building served as the residence of the prime minister in 1965-85, was rebuilt in 1993 and since it houses the national gallery, showcasing paintings and sculptures of Guyanese…
On a rainy day worth a visit. It has recorded guiding in English and a collection of Medieval and Renaissance Christian art.

Guided rafting trips on the Arno through the historic centre, passing beneath Ponte Vecchio. Tours last about one hour, require no previous experience and are run in inflatable rafts with an instructor in each boat.
Ambato's botanical gardens

The castle perched upon a hill in the middle of the city around which Graz sprang up. The funicular (Schloßbergbahn) (10-day and tourist tram/bus ticket covers the ride), and elevator (Schloßberglift) (€2) will take the effort…
An ancient convent where you can see the uncomfortable stone slabs where nuns slept, religious artwork, and, most importantly, a creepy underground crypt filled with mummified nuns.

A six-sided pavilion built in honor of Ui-sang Daesa, the founder of Naksansa Temple, where he used to sit in meditation. The sunrise at Uisangdae is regarded as one of the most spectacular sights on the East Sea.
